  *****NOTE FROM THE CITY*****

Doors to the City Council Chamber will open at 1:30 p.m. for Open Session. Please be mindful that
seating is limited and available on a first come, first served basis.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City provides the following two alternative methods of viewing and listening to the City Council Meeting
convenience:

  ¡  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider
  for details.
  ¡  Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video,
  at https://www.facebook.com/cityofinglewood/

The disruption in service of any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body
from taking further action on an agenda item.

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City
Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit
comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments receiv
after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the
meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
 comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments receiv
after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the
meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

ACCESSIBILITY: If requested, the agenda and backup materials will be made available in appropriate
alternative formats to persons with a disability, as required by Section 202 of the Americans with Disabilities A
1990 (42 U.S.C. Sec. 12132), and the federal rules and regulations adopted in implementation thereof. Any
person who requires a disability-related modification or accommodation, or translation services in order to observe
and/or offer public comment may request such reasonable modification, accommodation, or service by contact
the Office of the City Clerk by telephone at 310-412-5280,  FAX at 310 -412-5533, One Manchester
Boulevard, First Floor, Inglewood City Hall, Inglewood, CA 90301 or via email
to athompson@cityofinglewood.org and aallen@cityofinglewood.org no later than 24 hours prior to the scheduled
meeting.

Inglewood, California
  June 4, 2024

  The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
  June 4, 2024, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

  Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
  Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the hour
  of 2:00 p.m.
  The City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary announced the
  presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority
  Chairman Butts, Council Members/Successor Agency
  Members/Housing Authority Members Gray, Padilla,
  Morales, Faulk; and
  Absent:  None.
  City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Mark F. Weinberg  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Derald Brenneman  Acting City Attorney/Acting General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Angela Allen  Deputy City Clerk

  * Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

  PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
  Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
  who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any item
  on the Agendas, other than the public hearings.

  There was no response.

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member
  /Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Faulk, and seconded by Council
  Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Morales that the demands
  presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated May 31, 2024, in
  the amount of $4,778,408.78, and dated May 23, 2024, in the amount of $1,263,786.67, are
  hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor Agency Secretary/Housing Authority
  Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said registers that said demands are so
  approved. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  PUBLIC HEARING CONTINUED – PLANNING COMMISSION’S DENIAL OF
  SPECIAL USE PERMIT NO. 23-00027. The City Clerk announced the next scheduled
  matter was a public hearing to consider an appeal by Erika Diaz (applicant) of the Planning
  Commission’s denial of Special Use Permit No. 23-00027 to allow the sale of beer and wine
  for off-site consumption at 3535 West Imperial Highway.

  The City Clerk announced that at the request of the applicant, that Agenda Item No. PH-1
  be continued to the City Council Meeting of July 23, 2024.

  Mayor Butts ordered the public hearing to be continued to the Council Meeting of July 23,
  2024, at the hour of 2:00 p.m.
 June 4, 2024

131.8  PUBLIC HEARING HELD – 2024-2025 ANNUAL ACTION PLAN. The City Clerk
  announced that the next scheduled matter was a public hearing to consider the priority
  community development, housing, and non-housing needs of low-and moderate-income
  residents for the development of the 2024-2025 Annual Action Plan, and that notices were
  given in the time, form, and manner as required by law, an affidavit was on file, and no
  communications were received.

  Mark F. Weinberg, City Manager, presented the Staff Report dated June 4, 2024.

  Roberto Chavez, HUD Programs manager, presented a brief oral presentation.

  Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present that wished to address the City
  Council on this matter.

  There was no response.

  Mayor Butts closed the public comment portion at the hour of 2:08 p.m.

142  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – L.A. DOOR CO. Staff report dated June 4, 2024, was
  presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members authorize payment of an
  invoice submitted by L.A. Door Co. for door repair in the Finance Department Conference
  Room.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby authorize payment in the amount of $5,500. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  SUBAWARD AGREEMENT NO. 24-238 APPROVED – CITY OF LOS ANGELES.
  Staff report dated June 4, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council
  Members approve a subaward agreement with the City of Los Angeles for acceptance of
  FY 2023-2024 Urban Area Security Initiative (UASI) Grant Program Funds in the amount
  of $226,445.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby approve subaward Agreement No. 24-238. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

178  PURCHASE AUTHORIZED – AMERICAN BIKE PATROL SERVICES;
  RESOLUTION NO. 24-76 - AUTHORIZING FUNDS TO PURCHASE ELECTRIC
  BICYCLES AND AMENDING THE 2023-2024 FISCAL YEAR BUDGET. Staff
  report dated June 4, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council
  Members authorize the purchase of two (2) electric bicycles from American Bike Patrol
  Services.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Authorize purchase in a total amount not to exceed
  $9,999.97; and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 24-76 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AUTHORIZING THE USE OF $9,999.97 IN AIR QUALITY
  MANAGEMENT DISTRICT FUNDS TO PURCHASE ELECTRIC BICYCLES
  AND AMENDING THE 2023-2024 FISCAL YEAR BUDGET

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  2
 June 4, 2024

183  MASTER SERVICE AGREEMENT NO. 24-239 APPROVED – ENERWISE
  GLOBAL TECHNOLOGIES, LLC DBA CPOWER. Staff report dated June 4, 2024,
  was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members approve a Master
  Service Agreement with Enerwise Global Technologies, LLC dba CPower to serve as a
  Curtailment Service Provider for Southern California Edison’s (SCE) California
  Independent System Operator (CAISO) Resource Adequacy (RA) Program through
  December 31, 2024.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby approve Master Service Agreement No. 24-239. The motion
  was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

183  CONTRACT AWARDED AND AGREEMENT NO. 24-240 APPROVED –
  GRIFFITH COMPANY; RESOLUTION NO. 24-77 ADOPTED - AMENDING THE
  FISCAL YEAR 2023-24 OPERATING BUDGET. Staff report dated June 4, 2024, was
  presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members award a contract and
  approve an agreement with Griffith Company, for the I-405 Inglewood Gateway Landscape
  Project, per Bid No. CB-24-01.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Award contract and approve Agreement No. 24-240 in an
  amount not to exceed $589,999 (including a ten percent (10%) contingency amount of
  $58,999.90 for a total cost of $648,998.90); and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 24-77 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE FISCAL YEAR 2023-24 BUDGET TO
  AUTHORIZE THE USE OF $648,998.90 FROM THE GENERAL FUND FOR
  THE I-405 LANDSCAPE GATEWAY PROJECT

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

101  FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024 MID-YEAR BUDGET REVIEW REPORT RECEIVED
  AND FILED; RESOLUTION NO. 24-78 ADOPTED - AMENDING THE 2023-24
  FISCAL YEAR ANNUAL BUDGET IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE MIDYEAR
  BUDGET REVIEW. Staff report dated June 4, 2024, was presented presenting the Fiscal
  Year 2023-2024 Midyear Budget Review Report.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby: 1) Receive and file the Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Mid-Year
  Budget Review; and 2) Adopt Resolution No. 24-78 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, AMENDING THE 2023-24 ANNUAL BUDGET IN
  ACCORDANCE WITH THE MIDYEAR BUDGET REVIEW

  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Keauonna Buckhanon, Budget Manager, presented the Mid-Year Budget review for the
  Fiscal Year 2023-2024.

  3
 June 4, 2024

173  ORDINANCE NO. 24-06 ADOPTED – ESTABLISH PAY RANGE ASSIGNMENT
  AND CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT FOR FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024. Staff
  report dated June 4, 2024, was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council
  Members adopt Ordinance No. 24-06, establishing pay range assignments and conditions
  of employment for Fiscal Year 2023-2024.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  further reading be waived. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Thereupon, it was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member
  Faulk that Ordinance No. 24-06 entitled:

  AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA,
  ESTABLISHING PAY RANGE ASSIGNMENT AND CONDITIONS OF
  EMPLOYMENT FOR THE VARIOUS OFFICERS, EMPLOYEES AND
  POSITIONS IN THE SERVICE OF THE CITY FISCAL YEAR 2023-2024;
  INCLUDING THE INGLEWOOD TRANSIT CONNECTOR (ITC) GRANT
  FUNDED TRANSITIONAL APPOINTMENTS AND REPEALING ALL
  PREVIOUS ORDINANCES OF THE CITY IN CONFLICT OR AT VARIANCE
  HEREWITH; THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF INGLEWOOD,
  CALIFORNIA, DOES ORDAIN AS FOLLOWS:

  which was introduced at the meeting held on May 21, 2024, be adopted. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  REPORTS – CITY CLERK. City Clerk Aisha L. Thompson thanked Christine Padilla
  and Destinee Wesley for stepping in while she and Angela Allen were away at the
  International Institute of Municipal Clerks Conference in Canada. She thanked Christine
  and Destinee for doing a great job while she was away. The City Clerk thanked everyone
  who helped with the Women Rock Empowerment Summit. She stated that she knew
  Councilwoman Faulk and Councilwoman Gray gave their thanks. She sincerely thanked
  Councilwoman Faulk for working with her for three years on such a fantastic event. The City
  Clerk mentioned the 180 women who attended the summit and stated it was due to
  outstanding teamwork. She also mentioned the pleasure of working with Councilwoman
  Gray and thanked her for her kindness and diligence in providing the needed information for the
  summit. The City Clerk thanked Danny in the print shop, Elsa and Abby in Public  Works,
  and the Administration, Traffic, Purchasing, and Finance Departments. She also commended
  Thomas Uwal, the Parks and Recreation Department, Baz, and the senior center staff for their
  assistance. Additionally, she acknowledged Malcolm, Councilwoman  Faulk’s assistant, and
  her staff, Angela, Christine, Destinee, and Chieree. Finally, the City  Clerk thanked the
  speakers, presenters, vendors, sponsors, and Inglewood residents for  supporting  the
  Women Rock Empowerment Summit.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who wished
  to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not elsewhere
  considered on the Agenda.

  There was no response.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
  adjourned in the honor of the 8th Year dedication of the Willie Agee Playhouse, at the hour
  of 2:49 p.m.

  4
 June 4, 2024

  Approved this 27th day of August, 2024.
  _________________________
  Aisha L. Thompson, City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
